title: Derived Hom from a semidualizing complex detects bounded coherent isomorphisms
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Work in its ordinary module derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with $R\operatorname{Hom}$ as the internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. Write $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$ for objects with bounded, finitely generated cohomology. Let $C\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$ and assume the scalar-action morphism $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,C)$ is an isomorphism. For every $Z\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$, the equality $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,Z)=0$ implies $Z=0$. Consequently, for any morphism $f:X\to Y$ with $X,Y\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$, if $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,f)$ is an isomorphism then $f$ is an isomorphism. No finite projective or injective dimension of $C$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent corollary of Tag 0BFR (complete Noetherian local rings have dualizing complexes) and Tag 0A7C (duality on coherent complexes, including unbounded coherent complexes), using more-algebra.tex Tags 0A6A (flat RHom base change), 0A65 (tensor-Hom adjunction), and derived Nakayama. Proof of the corollary is explained in report.md; it is not asserted to be the statement of Tag 0A7C.

proof.text: Suppose $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,Z)=0$. For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, use the complete Noetherian local flat test ring $B_{\mathfrak m}$ supplied by [lem-trf-completed-maximal-localizations-detect-zero]. Apply [lem-trf-flat-coherent-homothety-base-change] to $A\to B_{\mathfrak m}$. It gives $C_B,Z_B\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(B)$, $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(C_B,Z_B)=0$, and the actual scalar-action isomorphism $B\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_B(C_B,C_B)$. If $C_B=0$, represent its first Hom argument by the zero complex: the defining Hom complex [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is zero in every degree, so $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(C_B,C_B)=0$. The transported scalar-action isomorphism would make the complex $B[0]$ zero in $D(B)$; taking degree-zero cohomology gives the zero module $B$, hence $1_B=0_B$, contrary to the nonzero test-ring clause. Hence $C_B\ne0$.

source.place: Agent assembly of the returned flat-change and localization/completion arguments, steps 1--2 and 5--7.

proof.text: For every such $B=B_{\mathfrak m}$ the complete-local nonzero-Hom detection lemma [lem-trf-complete-local-nonzero-rhom-detection] applies to $C_B,Z_B$ and gives $Z_B=0$. The joint zero-detection assertion of [lem-trf-completed-maximal-localizations-detect-zero] then gives $Z=0$. If $A$ is the zero ring, the latter assertion applies with no maximal ideals and still gives $Z=0$.

source.place: Agent assembly of returned steps 3--7: coherent duality and local tensor nonvanishing, followed by descent.

proof.text: Finally let $f:X\to Y$ be as in the statement and choose its distinguished cone triangle $X\to Y\to T\to X[1]$ in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives short exact sequences $0\to\operatorname{coker}H^i(f)\to H^i(T)\to\ker H^{i+1}(f)\to0$. The kernel is a submodule of the finite $A$-module $H^{i+1}(X)$, so it is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] since $A$ is Noetherian; the cokernel is generated by the images of generators of $H^i(Y)$. Lift generators of the kernel to $H^i(T)$ and adjoin the images in $H^i(T)$ of generators of the cokernel to obtain a finite generating set. If the cohomology of $X,Y$ is supported in $[a_X,b_X],[a_Y,b_Y]$, respectively, the same sequence makes $H^i(T)=0$ outside $[\min(a_Y,a_X-1),\max(b_Y,b_X-1)]$. Thus $T\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$.

source.place: Agent cone argument; derived-category cohomology exactness.

proof.text: Exactness in the second variable of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] sends the cone triangle to a distinguished triangle whose first arrow is $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,f)$. Since that arrow is an isomorphism, [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,T)=0$. The object-detection result just proved applies to this bounded-coherent $T$, hence $T=0$. Applying the same cone criterion to the original triangle gives that $f$ is an isomorphism.
